source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X, termwise cokernel argument

proof.text: Evaluation preserves cokernels. Identify each component of the ambient cokernel with the cokernel of the corresponding component of alpha using PreservesCokernel.iso. Apply coherent_kernel_cokernel_sum for cokernel closure and isomorphism invariance to obtain coherence of every component.

Prove the general multiplication-image cancellation lemma in any abelian monoidal closed category: for an epimorphism q:F to Q, a map f:Q to H kills the image of J tensor Q to Q if and only if q followed by f kills the image of J tensor F to F. Cancel both image factorizations. Tensor-left preserves epimorphisms by its right adjoint; cancel tensor-left(q), and apply left-unitor naturality and whisker exchange. Specialize this lemma to scheme modules using their existing monoidal closed structure. This replaces the three duplicated private sheaf-module helpers with one genuinely more general proved lemma.

The components of the ambient cokernel projection q are epimorphisms because evaluation preserves colimits. Apply the cancellation lemma to q_n and the identity: annihilation of G_n by I^(n+1) forces its product inclusion into Q_n to be zero. That inclusion is mono, so the ideal product is zero.

Fix adjacent levels and let p:Q_(n+1) to Q_(n+1)/I^(n+1)Q_(n+1). Naturality of q and the quotient description of the G transition show that Q transition kills the ideal product, giving a map a from this quotient to Q_n by cokernel.desc. The cancellation lemma shows that q_(n+1) followed by p kills the ideal product in G_(n+1); descend through its quotient and the given G quotient isomorphism to a map v:G_n to the quotient of Q_(n+1). The F transition is epi, and naturality of alpha shows alpha_n followed by v is zero. The evaluated ambient cokernel cofork is colimiting, so v descends to b:Q_n to the quotient of Q_(n+1). Cancel p and q_(n+1) to prove a followed by b is the identity. Cancel q_n and the epi G transition to prove b followed by a is the identity. The cokernel descent equation gives p followed by a equal to the Q transition, exactly the required adic condition.

title: Canonical cokernels of coherent formal modules
statement: For a Noetherian scheme X, ideal sheaf I, and morphism α between two coherent formal module inverse systems F and G, the ambient cokernel inverse system cokernel α is coherent formal.

lean.statement: theorem coherentFormalModules_canonicalCokernel_isCoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) {F G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules} (hF : IsCoherentFormalModule I F) (hG : IsCoherentFormalModule I G) (α : F ⟶ G) : IsCoherentFormalModule I (cokernel α)
